---
name: The Real World
one_sentence: 400 years after the Institute went silent — green, vast, indifferent.
---

## Description

A world reclaimed by nature. The Institute's buildings still stand, but they are crumbling, overgrown with vines and moss. The sky is real — vast, changing, sometimes grey, sometimes blindingly blue. The air smells of earth and rain and decay. It is beautiful and terrifying in equal measure.

## History

When the Institute sealed itself, the outside world was dying. But four hundred years is a long time. The planet healed. The humans who couldn't enter the Institute perished, but the world they left behind grew green and wild. The children who emerge from The I will find a world that doesn't need them — one that has moved on.

## Conflict

The real world is not hostile, but it is indifferent. It will not welcome the children, nor will it reject them. They will have to learn to live in a world that was never designed for them — a world where nothing appears when hunger strikes, where the light is not always correct, where survival is not guaranteed.
